subject: Civil Engineering
title: Levees and Flood Walls
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Levees and Flood Walls.

hook.text: New Orleans sits below sea level. Only levees keep the Mississippi from swallowing the city.

buildup.text: Levees are earthen embankments along rivers. Flood walls are concrete barriers in tight spaces.

discovery.text: Seepage through and under levees is the biggest failure risk — piping erodes them inside.

twist.text: Hurricane Katrina breached 50 levees in 2005. Over 1,800 people died.

climax.text: The $14 billion post-Katrina system added storm surge barriers and pumping stations.

punchline.text: Levees protect millions, but they must never fail — because failure is catastrophic.

quiz.question: What is the most common internal failure mechanism of levees?
options: Earthquake liquefaction of the levee soil
Seepage and piping — water erodes soil pathways through or under the levee
Overtopping from waves crashing over the levee crest
